title: Region bounds, error margins and certified positivity in the numerical conformal bootstrap; Or the first mathematically rigorous bounds on the 3d Ising CFT critical exponents
abstract: Numerical conformal bootstrap bounds are commonly called rigorous, yet as published they are not theorems: they hold at sampled points rather than on regions of parameter space, for truncated rational approximations of the conformal blocks, for a finite list of spins, and up to floating-point rounding. We close all four gaps. We show how to search efficiently for functionals positive on regions, including external-dimension space; how positivity on the large-spin crossing vectors can be imposed as such a region constraint; how new analytic bounds on the conformal-block recursion relations give functionals positive on the true, untruncated crossing vectors; and how to certify the positivity of these functionals in exact arithmetic. The certification rests on Bernstein-basis positivity certificates in up to three variables, exact arithmetic in $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt2)$, a compactified treatment of the infinite spin tail, and an explicit bound on the difference between the true blocks and their truncations, so that infinitely many positivity conditions reduce to finitely many machine-checked sign conditions. As a flagship application we certify an exclusion region in the $(Δ_σ,Δ_ε)$ plane: for $Δ_σ\in[0.505,0.5405]$ all of $Δ_ε\in(1/2,3]$ is excluded except a small rectangle containing the 3d Ising island, giving rigorous two-sided bounds on the critical exponents $η$ and $ν$ under explicitly stated spectrum assumptions. The analytic inputs for the mixed $σ$-$ε$ system, which would remove the spin-2 gap assumption, are also proved. The same methods prevent common practical failure modes and can make bootstrap searches faster: region bounds turn the mapping of an island into a handful of one-dimensional bisections. The essential code to reproduce the search and the certification, and all machine-checkable certificates, are released.
summary: This work provides the first mathematically rigorous bounds on the critical exponents of the 3D Ising CFT by upgrading the numerical conformal bootstrap. The authors overcome limitations in previous methods—such as relying on sampled points or floating-point arithmetic—by implementing exact arithmetic and region-based positivity certificates. This establishes a new standard for theoretical rigor in critical phenomena studies.
main_problem: To elevate numerical conformal bootstrap bounds from mere sampled points to mathematically rigorous theorems.
main_result:
The authors certify exclusion regions in the critical exponent parameter space $(\Delta_\sigma, \Delta_\epsilon)$, providing rigorous two-sided bounds on the 3D Ising CFT critical exponents $\eta$ and $
u$.
method: The methodology involves developing a multi-stage certification pipeline using exact arithmetic (in $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{2})$), Bernstein-basis positivity certificates, and careful handling of infinite spin tails and truncation errors.
model_or_system: The study focuses on the 3D Ising Conformal Field Theory (CFT), analyzing its four-point correlation function $\langle\sigma\sigma\sigma\sigmaangle$ via crossing-symmetry equations.
key_observables:
Critical exponents ($\eta$ and $
u$), and the parameters $(\Delta_\sigma, \Delta_\epsilon)$ defining the conformal block spectrum.
important_parameters: The parameter space $(\Delta_\sigma, \Delta_\epsilon)$ and the specific values of the critical exponents.
main_assumptions: The certification relies on a 'trusted computing base' of axioms and the assumption that the 3D Ising CFT is indeed conformal, though uniqueness is not proven.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate how point-based sampling can fail to capture true allowed regions, and how region bounds provide superior constraints compared to older point-based charting methods.
paper_structure: The paper systematically addresses four gaps in previous work (points vs. regions, finite vs. infinite spins, approximations vs. true blocks, floating point vs. exact arithmetic) before applying the full rigorous machinery to the 3D Ising model.
why_interesting: While focused on CFT, the rigorous mathematical techniques developed for certifying positivity on continuous parameter regions and handling infinite sums are highly relevant to bounding parameters in quantum field theories and critical phenomena.

The true underlying allowed shape is shown in green. The figure shows how sampling at a finite number of points can miss isolated allowed islands as well as thin protrusions that stick out in between the sampled points. This could result in wildly inaccurate bounds if the true CFT is located inside the unsampled island or an unsampled protrusion! Figure 2: Numerical conformal bootstrap bounds obtained in [5] (light-blue) compared against a version re-computed in [6] using more compute and newer methods (darker blue). This illustrates an explicit example where the conventional point-based ‘charting’ approach led to bounds that were later found to be too strong. The figure on the right illustrates how region bounds can be used to prevent such mistakes in the future: A fully closing ring on all sides would certify bounds regardless of the shape of the island (or islands!).
